items.name: narration_en
items.direction: Narrate this for a premium documentary YouTube Shorts channel about money, history and the tricks behind them. The Narrator is a deep, warm, confident storyteller with a hint of mystery: curious, quietly amused, energetic and punchy, never slow, never announcer-like. Natural emphasis on dates and numbers, questions end with a curious lift, a short comic pause before each punchline. Keep the same voice, pace and energy from start to finish. Chars voices two funny cartoon characters (a smug gold bar and a nervous banknote), short and punchy, performed exactly as described in each bracket.
lines: Narrator
Your safe haven just lost twenty-eight percent from its record, in the middle of a war. Why is gold falling?
Narrator
This week, attacks on Saudi oil sent Brent crude to a hundred and twelve dollars. Stocks are sliding.
Chars
[smug, deep, rich gold bar, very pleased with himself] Relax. This is my moment.
Narrator
Then gold dipped below four thousand dollars.
Narrator
So why does the shield crack exactly when you need it?
Narrator
First, gold pays you nothing. A US government bond pays about five percent.
Narrator
Oil means inflation. Inflation means rates stay high. And holding nothing gets expensive.
Chars
[delighted, squeaky nervous banknote, surprised to be winning] For once, paper wins!
Narrator
Second, when stocks crash, people sell what they can, not what they love. Gold is the cash machine.
Narrator
That's the mirage: gold isn't a crisis shield. It's mostly a bet that rates will fall.
Narrator
So when a crisis pushes rates up... your safe haven isn't.
Chars
[sulking, deep, wounded pride, lying face down] I'm not falling. I'm resting.
Narrator
This is Money Mirage. Follow for more.
